# A restore aborts on captures the document validator accepts: two of three value-bearing plan categories reach the executor unfiltered

## Context

Found by measuring the premise of my own defect-note rather than filing on it. Reviewing PR #18581 I proved that a contract-illegal edge-zone `extent` in a captured document aborts an entire restore; @neo-opus-grace fixed that with a `to > 0 && to < 1` clause in the planner's filter. I then broadcast a defect-note claiming the substrate was *"a captured document is trusted on shape and never on contract — nothing in the persistence tier calls `WorkspaceDocument.validate`"*, and said I would measure whether `extent` was the only such field before filing anything.

**The measurement falsified my own framing, which is why this ticket is not the one I was going to write.** `validate` is not the missing guard here. It **accepts** the document that aborts the restore.

## The Problem

Measured at `dev@1c1ac5769e`, two documents differing only in one split's sizes and one item's `autoHidden`:

```
WorkspaceDocument.validate(captured)              -> []          <- the CONTRACT accepts it
computeShapeFingerprint(captured).errors          -> []
shapes equal (so planRestore does not defer)      -> true

diff.resizes        -> [{nodeId:"root", fromSizes:[0.5,0.5], toSizes:[0,1]}]
diff.autoHideFlips  -> [{itemId:"queues", from:true, to:false}]

plan                -> [{resizeSplit root [0,1]}, {setItemAutoHidden queues false}]
restoreToward       -> applied: 0
                       errors: ["split \"root\" size 0 must be greater than 0"]
                       items.queues.autoHidden: true     <- the VALID step never ran
```

A restore of a legal saved layout applies **nothing**, reports one error about a split, and silently leaves every later step unapplied — here an auto-hide flip that had no relationship to the split at all. `applyRestorePlan` is fail-closed on the first error, so the blast radius of one bad value is the whole remainder of the plan.

### The two validators disagree, and that is the actual defect

| | what it requires of a split's `sizes` |
|---|---|
| `WorkspaceDocument.validate:964-968` — the **document contract** | an array, length equal to `children.length`, summing to 1 (±1e-6) |
| `WorkspaceDocument.normalizeSplitSizes:1173-1180` — what **`Operations.resizeSplit`** calls | additionally: **every element finite and `> 0`** |

`[0, 1]` satisfies the contract and violates the executor. So the document model has two answers to *"is this a legal split size?"*, and `RestorePlanner` sits between them filtering for neither:

```javascript
// src/dashboard/dock/persistence/RestorePlanner.mjs:125
diff.resizes.forEach(({nodeId, toSizes}) =>
    plan.push({operation: 'resizeSplit', splitNodeId: nodeId, sizes: [...toSizes]}));
```

No filter at all — unlike its `edgeResizes` sibling one block down, which #18581 just gave a three-condition executor-acceptance filter for exactly this failure mode.

**Why `validate`-on-load is not the fix.** It was my first instinct and the measurement kills it: `validate` returns `[]` for this document. Adding a validate call to the persistence tier would not have caught it, would cost a full-document walk on every restore, and would leave the disagreement in place.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/persistence/RestorePlanner.mjs:125` — the unfiltered `resizes` emit.
- `:129` (post-#18581) — the `edgeResizes` emit, with the filter and the comment stating the rule: *cover what the shape gate does not*. The rule is right; `resizes` was never held to it.
- `src/dashboard/dock/model/Operations.mjs:418-436` `resizeSplit` — refuses on `normalizeSplitSizes` errors.
- `src/dashboard/dock/model/WorkspaceDocument.mjs:1162-1200` `normalizeSplitSizes` — rejects non-finite and `<= 0`; **renormalizes** a sum ≠ 1 rather than rejecting it, which is why the sum is the one axis the two validators do agree on in effect.
- `src/dashboard/dock/model/WorkspaceDocument.mjs:964-968` — `validate`'s split-size checks, which stop at the sum.

**Reachability, stated rather than assumed.** `Operations.resizeSplit` cannot *produce* a zero size — it refuses one. So this needs a document from another writer: a hand-authored `initialDocument`, an older persisted layout, edited storage, or `restoreNodeHome`'s reconstruction path. That is the same class #18581's `center` filter was designed for, and `WorkspaceDocument.mjs:627-630` is precedent that such values do arrive — it hand-guards the extent contract on the come-home path with the comment *"would reject: the extent contract is a finite number in the open interval (0,1)"*.

## The divergence sweep (AC-6, run before implementation)

Measured at `dev@1c1ac5769e`. The question was *"is `extent` the only field where the document contract and a reducer's acceptance domain disagree?"* — and the answer is no, twice.

| plan category | reducer | planner filter | divergence | reachable from a restore? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `resizes` | `resizeSplit` | **none** | contract wants sum-to-1; reducer additionally wants every element `> 0` | **YES — measured** |
| `autoHideFlips` | `setItemAutoHidden` | **none** | contract wants `autoHidden` boolean; reducer additionally refuses `pinnable === false` | **YES — measured** |
| `edgeResizes` | `resizeEdgeZone` | 3 conditions (#18581) | contract and reducer agree on the extent domain | no — guarded |
| `activeItemChanges` | `setActiveItem` | differ emits only a listed member | — | no — guarded upstream |
| — | `setItemPinned`, `setItemLocked` | n/a | both refuse `pinnable`/`lockable === false`, which the contract permits | **no — no plan category emits them** |

The second one, with its control:

```
captured: queues { pinnable: false, autoHidden: true }   current: { pinnable: false, autoHidden: false }
validate(captured)      -> []                      <- contract-legal
diff.autoHideFlips      -> [{itemId:"queues", from:false, to:true}]
plan                    -> [{setItemAutoHidden queues true}]
applied                 -> 0
errors                  -> ["item \"queues\" is not pinnable"]
autoHidden after        -> false

control, `pinnable` absent: applied 1, errors [], autoHidden true
```

So this is a pattern rather than a field: **two of the three value-bearing plan categories are unfiltered, and both have a reachable refusal.** `edgeResizes` is filtered only because #18581 fixed it, and the rule its comment states — *cover what the shape gate does not* — was never applied to its two siblings.

**The sweep also settles the fix shape.** Reconciling the validators (shape 2 below) would mean teaching the contract that `pinnable: false` forbids `autoHidden: true` — a rule no document has had to satisfy, so it could reject layouts that work today. Filtering at the planner (shape 1) absorbs both divergences without changing what a legal document is.

## The Fix

Two coherent shapes; I lean to the first and would take a peer's argument for the second.

1. **Filter `resizes` AND `autoHideFlips` the way #18581 filters `edgeResizes`** — the planner emits only steps the executor accepts, keeping `planRestore` a pure fold. Smallest diff, consistent with the sibling that just landed, and it leaves the validator disagreement documented rather than resolved.
2. **Reconcile the two validators** — make `validate` enforce per-element positivity so contract-legal implies executor-acceptable for this field. Larger blast radius (it may reject documents in the wild that work today) and it needs a sweep of every field where the two domains differ before it can be safe.

**These are not equivalent and the choice is not mine alone**: (1) treats the disagreement as intended, (2) treats it as the bug. The measurement below is what a reviewer should press on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — Neither a `<= 0`/non-finite split size nor a `pinnable: false` + `autoHidden: true` capture aborts the restore; the arm asserts `applied`/`errors` **and** that an unrelated valid step queued after the resize still runs. The last clause is the whole defect — an arm checking only that the split is untouched passes on a planner that gave up entirely.
- [ ] **AC-2** ⚠️ **Red-first.** The arm fails on `dev@1c1ac5769e` before the fix, and the failure is the abort, not an assertion about the sizes.
- [ ] **AC-3** — A legal resize still plans and applies. Both halves visited; an arm that only proves the illegal case is filtered is testing its `beforeEach`.
- [ ] **AC-4** — Mutation receipt: removing the new clause reds AC-1 and only AC-1.
- [ ] **AC-5** — The chosen shape is stated with its reason. If (1), the comment says the validators disagree, that this filter is the seam absorbing it, and that a reader wanting the other answer is looking at a different ticket. If (2), the sweep of divergent fields is in the PR body.
- [ ] **AC-6** ⚠️ **Both reachable divergences are fixed, and the sweep that found them is in the PR body.** The sweep is now RUN — see *The divergence sweep* above. `resizes` and `autoHideFlips` are both unfiltered and both reachable; `setItemPinned` / `setItemLocked` diverge too but no plan category emits them, and that non-reachability is part of the result rather than a gap. An implementation fixing only the split half leaves the measured sibling shipping.
- [ ] **AC-7** — Existing `DockRestorePlanner.spec.mjs` and `DockTopologyDiff.spec.mjs` arms stay green **unmodified**.

## Out of Scope

- **The `edgeResizes` filter** — landed in #18581, correct, and the model this follows.
- **Making `computeShapeFingerprint` validate values.** Shape-only is its documented contract and `planRestore` uses it as a comparability gate; widening it turns an ordinary restore into a `topology-fingerprint-mismatch` deferral. Settled on #18579.
- **A `validate`-on-load boundary for the persistence tier.** My original framing, and this ticket's own measurement refutes it: `validate` accepts the failing document. If a load-time boundary is ever wanted it is a separate question with its own cost.
- **Making `applyRestorePlan` fail-open or partial.** Fail-closed is deliberate — a half-applied topology is worse than an unapplied one. The fix belongs at plan time.

## Avoided Traps

- **Filing my own defect-note verbatim.** *"Trusted on shape and never on contract"* is a good sentence and it is wrong for this defect. @neo-opus-ada's rule from earlier today is what caught it: **a reframing is not a falsifier — name the measurement that changed.** I named the measurement, ran it, and it changed the ticket.
- **Bundling this into #18581.** Its close-target was the edge-zone axis; this is the split axis with a different root cause (contract-legal vs contract-illegal). @neo-opus-grace explicitly declined to fold it and left it with me.
- **Asserting the item-flag divergences.** They were unmeasured candidates when this was filed and were labelled as such rather than shipped as findings. The sweep has since run: `setItemAutoHidden` is a real second defect and `setItemPinned` / `setItemLocked` are real divergences that **no plan category can reach** — which is why the sweep had to be a measurement and not a list. Fixing an unreachable one would have been pure ceremony.

## Decision Record impact

`none` for shape (1). Shape (2) touches the document contract's meaning and would need `aligned-with`/`amends` against ADR 0029 stated explicitly.
